newsitem.title: JAPAN: Stock moves to have indirect economic impact - MOF.
newsitem.headline: Stock moves to have indirect economic impact - MOF.

text.p: Japanese stock price movements will have an indirect impact on the economy, but their prices are set freely by the market and the government should not intervene, Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka told a parliamentary committee on Wednesday.
"(Stock prices) are set by free market forces," Mitsuzuka said.

Although he said the government should not intervene in the stock market, he said Japanese authorities would continue to watch the market closely as share prices have an indirect effect on the real economy.
He also said the government will take into account movements in stock prices when carrying out its future management of the economy.
"We will note of the stock prices and take it as a message toward the management of the economy," he said.
Although Tokyo shares staged a strong rebound on Wednesday, they had been battered recently due to pessimism over the outlook for the Japanese economy in the next fiscal year starting in April.
